<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par131 />{{GHGmargin-letter|131|s}}
6. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=33|verse=4}} ({{GHGheb|text=מֽוֹרָשָׁה}}, perhaps {{GHGheb|text=מוֹר׳ לִקְהִלַּת}} is to be read), 33:27 ({{GHGheb|text=מְעֹנָה}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=7|verse=8}} ({{GHGheb|text=צֵדָה}}), the absolute state appears to be used instead of the construct to govern a following logical genitive; this, however, cannot be explained either as a special kind of apposition, or (with Hitzig) as a peculiarity of the dialect of Northern Palestine, but is merely a textual corruption. On the other hand, in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=31|verse=11}} {{GHGheb|text=עָוֹן}} is evidently intended to combine the readings {{GHGheb|text=עֲוֹן פְּלִילִים}} and {{GHGheb|text=עָוֹן פְּלִילִי}} (as in verse 28).—The remarkable combination {{GHGheb|text=אֱלֹהִים צְבָאוֹת}} in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=80|verse=8}}, 15 is due to the fact that in ψψ 42–83 {{GHGheb|text=אֱלֹהִים}} has almost throughout been subsequently substituted by some redactor for the divine name {{GHGheb|text=יחוה}}; on {{GHGheb|text=יהוה צְבָאוֹת}} cf. {{GHGpar|125|h}}. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=59|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=80|verse=5|hidebook=1}}, 20, and 84:9 {{GHGheb|text=יהוה}} has been reinstated in the text before {{GHGheb|text=אֱלֹהִים צְבָאוֹת}}.<ref>Without this assumption it would be inconceivable that {{GHGheb|text=יהוה אֱלֹהֵי צְבָאוֹת}} should not have been written; that the anther of these Psalms regarded {{GHGheb|text=צְבָאֹוֹת}} already as an independent name of God (so Gesenius and Olshausen) is out of the question.</ref>

{{GHGmargin-letter|131|t}}
7. Lastly, the nearer definition (qualification) of a noun may be effected by means of a preposition (either with a suffix or with an independent noun), but must then be distinguished from the cases in which the preposition is dependent on a verb or verbal idea, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=3|verse=6}} ''and she gave also'' {{GHGheb|text=לְאִישָׁהּ עִמָּהּ|translate=unto her husband with her}} (= ''her husband who was with her''); in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=9|verse=16}} (''that I may remember the everlasting covenant between God and every living creature of all flesh'') and other places, the qualification of the noun is itself also qualified.<section end=par131 />

<section begin=par132 />{{GHGpar-heading|132|Connexion of the Substantive with the Adjective||<ref>On the expression of attributive ideas by substantives, cf. above, {{GHGpar|127|h}}, and {{GHGpar|128|o}}, with the note; {{GHGpar|135|n}} and {{GHGpar|141|c}} (substantives for adjectives as predicates of noun-clauses) and {{GHGpar|152|u}} (periphrases for negative qualities). On the use of the feminine of adjectives (and participles) to express abstract ideas, see {{GHGpar|122|q}}. It remains to mention further the employment (mostly only in poetry) of certain epithets in place of the substantives to which the quality in question belongs; e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אָבִיר|translate=the strong one}}, i.e. ''God''; {{GHGheb|text=אַבִּיר|translate=the strong one}}, i.e. ''the bull'' (in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=8|verse=16}}, &c., ''the horse''); {{GHGheb|text=קַל|translate=swift}}=''the runner'' (of the ''horse'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=30|verse=16}}); {{GHGheb|text=לְבָנָה|translate=alba}}, i.e, ''luna''; {{GHGheb|text=פֹּֽרִיָּה}} (''fructifera'') ''a fruitful tree'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=17|verse=6}} (so {{GHGheb|text=פֹּרָת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=49|verse=22}}); {{GHGheb|text=רֹבֵץ|translate=a croucher}}, i.e. ''a crouching beast of prey'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=4|verse=7}}. Cf. also {{GHGheb|text=רֹזֵן}} (''gravis, augustus'') and {{GHGheb|text=נָשִׂיא}} (''elatus'' ?), i.e. ''a prince''. The use of adjectives and participles for substantives is much more extensive in Arabic. In Greek and Latin poetical language cf. such examples as ὑγρή = ''the sea''; ''merum'' for ''vinum'', &c.</ref>}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|132|a}}
'''1.''' The adjective (like the participle used adjectivally), which serves as an ''attribute'' of a substantive, stands ''after'' the substantive, and agrees with it in ''gender'' and ''number'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ גָּדוֹל|translate=a great man}}, {{GHGheb|text=אִשָּׁה יָפָה|translate=a beautiful woman}}. If the substantive is immediately connected with a genitive, the attribute follows the latter, since, according to § 89 and {{GHGpar|128|a}}, the construct state and the genitive belonging to it are inseparably united, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=8|verse=15}} {{GHGheb|text=עֲטֶ֫רֶת זָהָב גְּדוֹלָה|translate=a great crown of gold}}.— On the attribute when attached to a ''determinate'' substantive, see above, {{GHGpar|126|u}}.
